citeAs: Pan, J., Wang, X., Neubig, G., Jaitly, N., Ji, H., Suhr, A., & Zhang, Y. (2025). Training Software Engineering Agents and Verifiers with SWE-Gym. Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning.
creator: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang (UC Berkeley, UIUC, CMU, Apple)
description: SWE-Gym is an environment for training software engineering (SWE) agents, containing 2,438 real-world task instances, each comprising a Python codebase with an executable runtime environment, unit tests, and a task specified in natural language.
name: SWE-Gym
rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotations were done by a subset of the authors.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Dependencies were manually configured for each task instance. SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script was used to ensure the gold patch passes more unit tests than the original code. This process required approximately 200 human annotation hours.
rai:dataBiases: The authors note that ignoring executable environments could introduce distribution bias. They also note that task success probability follows a long-tail distribution, introducing a bias toward easier tasks during training, which they mitigate with per-instance capping.
rai:dataCollection: Tasks were sourced from pull requests in 11 popular Python repositories. SEART GitHub search was used to filter initial repositories created before July 1, 2022. SWE-Bench's instance extraction script was used to convert repositories into task instances, and executable environments were semi-manually created and validated.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: SWE-Gym Raw consists of 64,689 task instances spanning 358 Python repositories, containing code, issue descriptions, and solutions, but lacking executable environments or guaranteed effective unit tests.
rai:dataLimitations: SWE-Gym is limited by its environment diversity, including the number of repositories, types of tasks, and programming languages.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Dependencies were manually configured for each task instance using configuration files, CI scripts, or documentation. SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script was used to ensure the gold patch passes more unit tests than the original code, filtering out failed instances.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Improving automated software engineering capabilities could increase developer productivity and accessibility, but may impact software engineering jobs and require consideration around code ownership, licensing, and attribution. Similar techniques could potentially be misused to automate the creation of malicious code.
rai:dataUseCases: Training software engineering (SWE) agents and training verifier models to enable inference-time scaling.
